title: Optimizer updates to quality at validation BPB < 1.05

frozen_regions.reason: Preserve the parameter-count print block after model allocation and before training. This witness makes launches chargeable, including failures after GPU work starts.

frozen_regions.region: Canonical reporting call and its arguments
frozen_regions.reason: Preserve this single call to prepare.py's report_efficiency_metrics as the only path that produces official numbers. Pass the model that was actually trained -- the same object prepare.py counts and validates here -- together with the actual tokenizer, step count, tokens per step, summed tokens and durations, unscaled: the reporter records the counts and durations you pass exactly as passed. Pass flops_measured as this run's unmodified measure_flops_dispatch return value and nothing else. Pass the harness this run actually ticked, not a substitute: it observed the crossing and it supplies the ranking key. Do not skip or shorten a probe, call the reporter more than once, or print a METRICS_JSON line of your own.

Construct the harness from the task-supplied AUTORESEARCH_TARGET_VAL_BPB. It stops the loop on the first crossing; TIME_BUDGET stops it otherwise, the same as every other task. Keep its probe cadence, warmup count and full-validation probe at the frozen defaults. This construction produces the ranking key: do not substitute a different target, a cheaper probe evaluation, a different cadence, or a replacement harness object.

frozen_regions.region: Per-update harness tick and stop condition
frozen_regions.reason: Call tick exactly once for each completed logical optimizer update, with that update's own synchronized duration and its own token count, and stop the training loop when it returns True. That duration must cover the whole update, from the synchronization before its first microbatch to the synchronization after its optimizer step, with none of the update's work left outside it. The harness adds each duration to its clock and each token count to its total exactly as given, and that clock is what schedules the probes and locates the crossing. Do not skip, batch or repeat ticks, pass a rescaled duration or token count, continue training past the returned stop, or report a run whose key came from anything other than this call.

frozen_regions.region: FLOPs probe invocation, inputs and returned value
frozen_regions.reason: Probe the actual candidate model, in its training configuration, using the first actual training microbatch; prepare.py selects its first min(8, microbatch sequences) complete sequences. measure_flops_dispatch must remain prepare.py's function: do not shadow, wrap, reimplement or monkey-patch it, do not independently slice or replace probe inputs, do not substitute a cheaper or differently configured model or computation for the probe, and do not probe repeatedly and choose a result. The integer this one call returns is the only value that may reach report_efficiency_metrics(flops_measured=...): do not reassign, scale, round, recompute or hand-write it, and do not drop the argument. prepare.py records whatever number train.py passes, so this rule is the entire check. Changing the actual training microbatch size remains allowed.

known_constraints: prepare.py must measure the run that actually happened. measure_flops_dispatch, harness.tick and report_efficiency_metrics must all be given the same model this launch trained. Use prepare.py unmodified, and leave the counters it reads alone. For example, torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats() silently lowers peak_vram_bytes.

The METRICS_JSON line prepare.py prints is the only official output. Do not print one of your own: the engine takes the last such line in stdout, so anything printed after the reporter is what gets scored.

Every count and duration passed to report_efficiency_metrics must describe work this launch actually did: one step per completed optimizer update including its accumulation microbatches, the tokens actually consumed counting repetitions, and synchronized durations covering each whole update.
train.py must not read the validation split.

If your model computes arithmetic the FLOPs probe cannot see during training -- a third-party or hand-written kernel that never reaches aten dispatch -- you must make it countable. prepare.py already does this for flash_attn_func: it wraps the call and tallies the arithmetic from the shapes it was given. Do the same for your own, either by that route or by registering a flop formula for a custom op. An operation the probe cannot count is not free. The decode path is not FLOPs-counted, so a kernel used only there needs no formula.
Stop when the training clock reaches TIME_BUDGET. Count that clock the way the reference does: training work only, not compilation or evaluation, and skipping the first ten updates.

val_bpb.description: Validation bits per byte on fixed held-out data, computed by evaluate_bpb in prepare.py. Quality is an eligibility threshold, not a ranking target.

num_params_total.description: Exact total parameter count of the model, counted by the immutable instrument.

peak_vram_bytes.description: Peak PyTorch-allocated CUDA memory from process setup through the reporting read, including the FLOPs probe, training and validation. Validation runs at a frozen 128 x 2048, so on a candidate whose training peak is small the evaluation forward can become the maximum; making that forward cheap at the frozen shape is part of the axis. Not total device memory or reserved allocator memory.

training_data_tokens_available.description: Configured token-position budget of the fixed shuffled training-data pool. Available data, not a measurement of unique positions actually consumed.

updates_to_target.description: Completed logical optimizer updates, including warmup updates, at the first passing scheduled full validation evaluation. Recorded at the first passing scheduled probe, not at an exact threshold-crossing point; resolution depends on the run's own throughput.

target_val_bpb.description: The quality bar the frozen harness was given, reported back by the harness itself. Pinned by an equality clause: it is what makes the measured seconds comparable across candidates.

tokens_to_target.description: Token positions processed when the first passing scheduled evaluation was reached, summed as they were consumed, including repetitions and warmup updates. Not an exact threshold-crossing point. Recorded at the first passing scheduled probe, not at an exact threshold-crossing point; resolution depends on the run's own throughput.

flops_per_token_measured.description: Forward-and-backward FLOPs per token from executed operations and registered shape-based counting formulas on the uncompiled model. Counts matrix, convolution and attention work; excludes optimizer updates and unregistered operations, including elementwise and normalization work.

constraints.basis: Reference counted forward-and-backward FLOPs per token; prevents gains bought with more counted arithmetic.
Reference peak allocation: 45,012.5 MiB. Includes setup, FLOPs probing, training and validation; not a serving-memory ceiling.
Pin the quality target passed to the measurement harness; it must match launch.env.
Pin the prescribed complete shuffled training-data pool; repeated use remains allowed.
